answer: Each identity claims a timber log, locks an 80-credit bond, and key-binds its pearl marker and onyx seal to it. The auditor measures length and end diameter, recomputes board-foot volume from the public log-scale table. A measurement whose volume deviates over 3%, whose pearl serial repeats, or whose onyx seal matches another key burns the bond. First fee 36, k-th 36+7(k-1), 1000th 7029; 1000 fakes pay 3,532,500 and lock 80,000. A rented-log ring fails: one pearl serial cannot certify two logs, while an honest identity pays 36 once and redeems its bond after a clean check.
